pages.scan: I opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/storyboards-unnumbered/page-04.png and looked at it myself before reading any source, script, workflow.json or guide. It has no numbers or flow lines. Grey boxes stand in for faces and there is no art. Layout: one wide panel across the top, then two tall panels side by side. Natural reading order: (1) Top panel, caption at top left: "Soon, his slot comes up." (2) Teal label at top right: "NOW · A-12". Between them, in the centre, is the 'ravi' face box. A small 'meera' face box sits at the far right below the label. Neither speaks, so these are silent beats. (3) Bottom-left tall panel, caption at top left: "A quick vitals check first." (4) Balloon below and to the right of it: "Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me." Its tail points down to the 'nurse' face box. The 'ravi' face box is lower left and silent. (5) Bottom-right tall panel, caption at top: "Dr. Ananya is notified when he's ready." The 'ananya' face box is mid-panel and silent. (6) Teal label near the bottom of that panel: "RAVI · READY". Page number: 4.
pages.observation: The order is unambiguous. Each panel has a single top-left caption, followed by at most one balloon or label. The top panel reads left to right, from the caption to the label, past Ravi's face box. The bottom row splits clearly into two full-height panels. The 04-2 caption and the 04-3 caption sit at almost the same height, so a reader could glance across the gutter. However, the nurse balloon sits right under the 04-2 caption and holds the eye inside the left panel. I found no skipped reply. The nurse's line needs no answer, and Ravi's reply can be a silent reaction. The tail clearly points to the nurse box, not to Ravi. 'he' in the 04-3 caption resolves to Ravi through the label below. In the storyboard, the RAVI · READY label floats far below the Ananya face box. No tablet is drawn, so I cannot judge here whether it will sit on a device. The label wraps as "RAVI ·" / "READY", leaving the middle dot at the end of a line, which is slightly awkward. Everything else is legible.
